newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul scandal seen hitting politicians, bureaucrats.
newsitem.headline: Seoul scandal seen hitting politicians, bureaucrats.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Sunday prepared to summon former or current politicians and government officials for questioning over a loan scandal surrounding the troubled Hanbo Group, local news reports said.

The state Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) radio said the focus of investigation was now placed on whether influence peddling was involved in the government approval of Hanbo Steel Co's construction of a new steel mill.
The report said there were also suspicions that banks had granted a huge amount of loans to the troubled steelmaker under pressure from politicians or government officials.
Prosecution officials could not immediately be reached.
None of the reports named any politicians and government officials expected to be summoned for questioning.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of the nation's sprawling Hanbo Group, racked up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans before it was declared insolvent on January 23.

Last week the prosecution arrested Sheen Kwang-shik, president of Korea First Bank, and Woo Chan-mok, head of Cho Hung Bank, on charges of taking bribes from Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo in return for loans.

Legislator Kwon Roh-kap of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics admitted last Wednesday to accepting between 150 million and 160 million won from Chung, partly to fund an election campaign.
He claimed that he had nothing to do with preferential loans to Hanbo and that he believed the money was "either political funds or rice cake money".
South Koreans traditionally swap small amounts of money, known as rice cake money, or gifts during major holidays as a token of friendship or respect.

He is the first politician to admit taking money from Chung, who built up the business conglomerate by rapidly expanding the steelmaking flagship and by acquiring or setting up 18 companies over the past three years.
It was not clear from news reports that Kwon would be summoned.
